qualification_limits: shared desktop and unequal client interfaces; short repeated runs are descriptive
latency percentiles include successes only; all failed/unexecuted offers reported separately
all overload loss and slow service cases disclosed; generic scan gains do not qualify durable tails
BIGINT aggregate subset; no raw projection, joins, updates/deletes or SQL transactions in Archive
no native Arrow/Parquet SDK; Parquet demo reads sources through DuckDB
receipt capacity correctness tested at 100000 IDs; long unique-write endurance unqualified
queue/cache budgets exclude caller allocations, active pinned pages and OS caches
backup/retention/orphan cleanup, upgrades and disk exhaustion remain unqualified
physical power loss, Windows directory-entry durability and Linux execution unqualified
no distributed scale, replication or TAOBench/Facebook-scale qualification
optional window bounds intentional collection waiting, not OS scheduling, queueing or ACK/storage time
coalescing can regress low concurrency, retries and tail latency; default remains zero
one-minute screens and descriptive repeats do not establish long endurance
unchanged storage/query checks inherited from prior proof are not counted as new tests
confirmed retries use an extra bounded receipt map; logical counter excludes BTree nodes and allocator overhead
fast retry successes acknowledge only original committed generations; pending IDs still use writer
favorable combined retry percentiles can hide slow new writes; operation-specific tails and losses retained
eight-second 10K retry screens and descriptive repeats do not establish sustained capacity
PreparedBatch amortizes library hashing only for immutable embedded reuse; unknown IDs copy/hash again at publication
millions of confirmed retries per second ingest zero new rows; no SQL/network/write capacity claim
prepared payload memory belongs to the caller; logical bytes exclude spare capacity and allocator overhead
SourceArchive coordinates one archive output and source interval; external source/other sinks are not transactional
source receipt history cannot advance empty output, reset sources, fence stale consumers or evict receipts
source publication comparison uses sequential matched canonical IDs; no causal durable-write speed improvement or current req/s qualification
older/generic writers must not publish reserved source IDs; format interoperability does not enforce typed source semantics
